title: Environment-aware entitlements and rate limits with chargeback and invoice-preview
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers operating multiple environments (dev, staging, prod) want separate entitlements, consistent rate-limit behavior, and clear chargeback visibility so platform teams can allocate costs and enforce guardrails without blocking developer workflows. Current entitlements are tenant-wide and lack environment context; teams workaround by creating separate tenants or manually tracking usage offline.
goals: Introduce environment-scoped entitlements (dev/staging/prod) per tenant so usage and quotas can be partitioned without creating separate accounts.
Support environment-aware rate-limits that can be stricter in non-prod (dev/staging) and more permissive in prod, configurable per plan and per-model.
Provide an invoice-preview and chargeback view that shows per-environment consumption, forecasted spend, and any soft-credit buckets applied.
Enable automatic promotion rules: when a team promotes resources from staging->prod, optionally transfer a one-time environment credit or update quotas according to policy.
non_goals: Not adding new pricing SKUs in this first rollout (we will map existing SKUs to environments).
Not implementing cross-tenant pooled entitlements (separate initiative).
Not building per-resource RBAC—this works with existing RBAC for environments but does not replace it.
requirements: API: New field 'environment' on metering and quota APIs with allowed values [dev, staging, prod]; default to 'prod' for backwards compatibility.
Console: Environment filter in usage and billing dashboards; toggle to view aggregated vs. per-environment metrics.
Quotas: Ability to set environment-specific quotas (token/month, calls/min) per plan and override per-customer.
Rate limits: Per-environment rate-limits that can be stricter than tenant-level defaults with clear precedence rules (environment-level > route-level > tenant default).
Soft credits: Add 'env_credit' bucket that can be auto-applied to offset charges for dev/staging usage up to configurable thresholds.
Invoice preview: Show line items grouped by environment with consumption, applied credits, and projected overage liabilities if thresholds breached.
Promotions: Admin API to transfer a configurable credit amount from staging->prod upon an explicit promote call; audit log entry required.
Backwards compatibility: Missing 'environment' field treated as 'prod' to ensure existing integrations continue to work.
Telemetry: Emit environment tag on all metering events and traces for cost attribution and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: API: Metering endpoint accepts 'environment' and persists it; create 3 test events for dev/staging/prod and verify stored events have correct tag.

Quotas: For a test tenant, set quotas: dev=10M tokens/month, staging=50M, prod=200M. Usage beyond dev quota should immediately trigger soft-limit behavior defined in spec (throttle + soft-credit application).
Rate limits: Configure route-level prod limit 100 req/s and dev limit 10 req/s. Under load test, dev requests above 10 req/s receive 429 with 'x-rate-limit-reason: env-quota-exceeded' header.
Console: Billing dashboard shows separate rows for dev/staging/prod with correct aggregated totals matching metering events for the same time window.

Invoice preview: Generate a preview for a tenant that uses 120M prod tokens, 60M staging tokens and 12M dev tokens, with a 20M dev credit. Preview must show applied credit to dev and math for projected overage on prod and staging.

Promotion API: Calling promote(env: 'staging' -> 'prod') with amount 5M creates a ledger entry, reduces staging credit by 5M, increases prod credit by 5M, and creates an audit log with actor and timestamp.
Backward compatibility: An existing ingestion client that omits 'environment' continues to have events counted as 'prod' and quotas behave unchanged.
Telemetry: At least one trace spans a request that hits rate-limit and includes environment tag; Cost-Analytics job can attribute spend to environments for the test tenant.
Security: Promotion action requires 'billing_admin' role; attempt by non-privileged user is rejected with 403.
implementation_notes: Schema change: Add environment enum column to meter_events table (nullable, default 'prod' for existing rows) — DB migration with backfill disabled for performance; existing rows treated as prod.
Quotas service: Extend quota key to include environment as part of the partition key. Existing caches invalidated on rollout.
Rate-limiter: Add precedence rules and ensure fast-path checks for common case where environment is prod to avoid perf regressions.
Console: Add environment selector to time-series queries; reuse existing charts but apply environment filter on query layer.
Billing: Invoice-preview uses metering snapshots and env_credit buckets; ensure edge cases (credit partial application) are tested.
Migration plan: Feature-flag rollout with default off; enable for internal pilot tenants, then invite-beta customers before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilot): Feature flag on for internal orgs; validate telemetry, quota behavior, and invoice-preview for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (beta customers): Enable by invite for 5 customers that requested multi-environment billing; collect feedback and adjust soft-credit policies.
Phase 3 (general availability): Gradual ramp to all tenants with communication and migration guide. Provide CLI tool to tag historical exported usage if customers opt-in.
open_questions: Should environment values be extensible (allow custom names) or locked to [dev, staging, prod]? Current proposal locks to three values for simplicity.
How do we present environments in multi-org teams with many project namespaces—do we add an environment per workspace or per project?
What is the exact precedence when both route-level and environment-level rate limits are configured and both would apply? (spec proposes environment-level wins).
Do we allow automatic rollover of unused dev credits to next month as 'dev buffer' or expire them?
